capability: Classify a CtrlRAM Base as AB only when two NVT markers are found, so longer Standard OSD Bases stay Standard
searchEvidence: Owner decision 2026-09-26: decide AB flash by whether two NVT markers can be found.

The complete NVT marker is 00 4E 56 54; a Standard image carries exactly one canonical NVT FWConfig Backup and an AB image one per bank. Today a single plausible bank (legacy single-candidate evidence) makes a 512 KiB NT51950 or a 1 MiB NT51951 Base AB when only one AB layout compiles at that length, which blocks their Display OSD Standard Bases.

OSD-AB-REFERENCE-CLASSIFICATION-1111-01 keeps a unique trusted AB structural proof terminal for damaged Backups and requires a 1 MiB non-AB image built from a Standard output and a tail to stay non-AB.
semanticOwner: FirmwareArtifactClassificationResolver remains the only CtrlRAM Base classification owner.
terminalContract: A CtrlRAM Base is AB when a published AB layout compiles at its length and either the existing unique trusted AB structural proof holds (damaged-Backup case of OSD-AB-REFERENCE-CLASSIFICATION-1111-01) or exactly one complete NVT marker (00 4E 56 54) is found inside each of that compiled layout's two canonical banks. Markers outside the canonical banks, such as in a Display OSD tail, never count. The legacy single-candidate evidence is retired: this owner decision supersedes the 1.1.11 requirement to keep NT51929/NT51951 single-candidate recognition. Bank issues (version bar, IC count, content plausibility) stay reported on an AB result but no longer decide the kind. Multiple equally evidenced candidates stay input.bank-reference.ambiguous and stale publications stay rejected. NumberToken never determines the kind. Without AB evidence the existing Standard/Unknown fallback applies. No profile, schema, contract, CRC or expected-byte change. Evidence: characterization of one marker, one per canonical bank, duplicate or tail markers, damaged-Backup structural proof and ambiguity, plus executed AB Golden cases.
